origin.description: Count how often each original observation appears in each bootstrap resample.

arguments.name: i.array
arguments.text: Integer matrix with R rows and n columns. Each row is one resample, and each entry is an index from 1 to n.

origin.details: Each row is counted with tabulate into bins 1 through n. A non-integer is truncated toward zero and counted only when that integer is between 1 and n. Missing values and non-positive values are skipped. A one-column matrix comes back as one row, because apply drops a length-one result before the transpose. An empty matrix comes back as 1 by 0.
origin.value: An integer matrix of counts. Column j says how often observation j appears in each resample.

translation.description: Count how often each original observation appears in each bootstrap resample.

arguments.name: i_array
arguments.text: Integer array with R rows and n columns. Each row is one resample, and each entry is an index from 1 to n.

translation.details: Each row is counted into bins 1 through n. A non-integer is truncated toward zero and counted only when that integer is between 1 and n. Missing values and non-positive values are skipped. A one-column matrix comes back as one row, matching R's apply. An empty matrix comes back as 1 by 0. The result is an int32 array.
translation.value: An integer matrix of counts. Column j says how often observation j appears in each resample.
translation.example:
from boot.util import freq_array

i_array = [[1, 2, 1, 3], [4, 2, 2, 1], [4, 3, 1, 2]]
print(freq_array(i_array))
